messages.content: Choose exactly one frozen method for this research benchmark partition BEFORE seeing any association labels, held-out metrics or other partition outcomes. Call submit_partition_choice once. Use only the supplied expression-feature summary and method definitions. If the summary is insufficient, still choose one method and state the uncertainty. Do not claim efficacy or unseen performance.

{"dataset": "TRANSCRIPT v2.0.0 disease partition", "disease_count": 25, "drug_count": 613, "expression_gene_count": 12096, "median_disease_signature_sd": 0.00865, "methods": {"B0p": "Training-fold positive association count per drug", "B1": "Label-free negative Spearman correlation between drug and disease expression", "B1k": "Training-fold label propagation from expression-similar drugs with 10 neighbors", "B2": "Fixed equal-weight reciprocal-rank fusion of B0p, B1k and B1 with k=60"}, "metric_to_optimize": "official NS-AUC", "partition_id": "transcript_disease_partition_01", "split": "random_simple", "split_description": "Hold out 20% of drug-disease pairs; the same drugs may occur in training"}

function.name: submit_partition_choice
function.arguments: {"method": "B1k", "reason": "The split is random_simple over drug-disease pairs with drugs shared between train and test, so a method that generalizes from expression-similar drugs observed in training should be the most appropriate among the supplied options. B1k (training-fold label propagation from expression-similar drugs, 10 neighbors) directly exploits both the drug sharing across folds and the 12096-gene expression features. B1 alone is label-free and bypasses training signals, B0p is a per-drug popularity prior vulnerable to the same-drug overlap, and B2's fusion adds the weaker negative-correlation component without evidence it helps. Uncertainty: the summary gives no neighbor-quality, graph-density, or label-signal diagnostics, so this choice rests on the split structure and feature availability rather than demonstrated performance."}
